newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan envoy to visit Americas to cement ties.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan envoy to visit Americas to cement ties.

text.p: Foreign Minister John Chang plans a three-week tour of Central America, hoping to bolster Taiwan's strong diplomatic ties in the face of mounting pressure from China, a local newspaper said on Monday.

The Foreign Ministry said Chang would attend a July meeting in Honduras with foreign ministers from seven Central American allies, but declined to confirm a United Daily News report that he would use the trip to conduct extensive regional visits.
A ministry spokesman denied reports that Chang would secretly visit unidentified South Pacific countries in May.

The United Daily News said Chang's Central American swing was intended to counter China's attempts to woo Taiwan's allies and pave the way for President Lee Teng-hui's attendance at an international conference in Panama in September.

Lee has accepted an invitation to attend a forum on the future of the Panama Canal, seen by diplomatically isolated Taiwan as a rare chance for meetings with world leaders. Communist China has regarded Nationalist-ruled Taiwan as a renegade province not entitled to international recognition since the two split after a civil war in 1949.
Taiwan lost a major diplomatic battle to China in 1996 when South Africa announced it would switch ties to Beijing in 1997.
Most of Taiwan's 30 diplomatic allies are underdeveloped nations in central America, Africa and the Pacific.
